To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synergistic effects on rat lung apparent collagen synthesis rates were observed when rats were exposed simultaneously to ozone (or nitrogen dioxide) and a respirable aerosol of ammoniurn sulfate.

the effects of O3 on lung collagen synthesis in vitro and on lung morphology are potentiated by exposure to a respirable aerosol of ammoniuim sulfate and that similar potentiation of O3 effects is observed in the presence of a respirable aerosols of sulfuric acid.
the response of the rat lung to exposure to ozone or nitrogen dioxide is potentiated by concurrent exposure to respirable-sized particles of ammonium sulfate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of oxidant air pollution on lung tissue.
the effects of oxidant air pollution (O3 and NO2) on the lung.
the effects of oxidant air pollution on the lungs of laboratory animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of ozone or NO2 in combination with (NH4)SO4 or sulfuric acid aerosols were synergistic, and not additive or multiplicative, in the sense that the effects of the two pollutants were greater when the two were combined.
the presence of a respirable aerosol, whether of ammonium sulfate or sulfuric acid, potentiates the effects of ozone or nitrogen dioxide on the rat lung.
exposure to a combination of oxidant air pollutant and respirable-sized aerosols may result in synergistic effects on rat lung collagen synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
synergistic effects on rat lung collagen synthesis rates were observed when mixtures of oxidants and respirable aerosol particles were inhaled.
the presence of respirable aerosols in the environment can potentiate the adverse effects of the oxidant air pollutant ozone, or of the acid aerosol sulfuric acid, on the lungs of rats.
the presence of respirable aerosols, such as (NH4) 2SO4, in the atmosphere, may enhance lung responses to oxidant gases, such as ozone or NO2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of aerosol can significantly alter the response of lungs to oxidant gases.
the synergistic effects we observed between the oxidant gases and the aerosol particles were not additive, but were instead supra-additive, and thus were synergistic.
the presence of a respirable aerosol may potentiate the effects of oxidant air pollution on the lungs.
